source.title: Route Sparse Autoencoder to Interpret Large Language Models
source.authors: Wei Shi; Sihang Li; Tao Liang; Mingyang Wan; Guo-Jun Ma; Xiang Wang; Xiang-Nan He

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; the supplied text contains the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE feature extraction and interpretation in an LLM, a setting different from the toy networks in the original source. It reports results on whether sparse dictionaries recover interpretable features from model activations.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own feature-count and interpretation-score evaluations, plus four specifically described RouteSAE features. The paper's citations to other work are not recorded as results. The feature-steering examples deliberately raise a selected feature's activation, so they are not evidence that the behavior occurs without inducement. The GPT-4o/human agreement analysis is not a direct test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units; routing-weight and reconstruction results do not test the geometry named in the claim.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It uses SAEs as a tool that 'reverses the effects of superposition' and benchmarks its own RouteSAE against ReLU, Gated, TopK, Crosscoder and random-routing baselines. It does so on feature counts, GPT-4o interpretation scores, KL divergence and reconstruction, all on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. It never asks whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recoverable as a test of the claim. There is no ground truth, no neuron-level polysemanticity measure, and no question of whether the model 'contains' the features. Every reported number compares SAE methods.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that RouteSAE's learned routing over layers 3–11 with a shared TopK SAE yields 22.5% more interpretable features and a 22.3% higher interpretation score than baseline SAEs at sparsity 64, with lower KL divergence, and enables targeted feature steering. They note that the router is simple and that cross-layer feature discovery is not yet optimized.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies toy networks and superposition geometry; this paper trains and evaluates TopK-based SAEs, including RouteSAE's learned routing across Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct residual-stream layers. It tests feature recovery and interpretation rather than toy-network feature overlap or geometric transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of retained features and interpretation scores are evaluated across sparsity levels; the feature-count analysis uses an activation threshold of 15, and the authors report a quantity-versus-interpretability trade-off as the threshold changes.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The experiments use one LLM checkpoint. Interpretation scores are based on 100 randomly selected features per SAE and GPT-4o scoring; the authors say these results are indicative rather than definitive because feature selection and GPT-4o scoring are stochastic. The paper notes that Crosscoder lacks complete experimental validation and that its comparison may not reflect its actual performance. It does not establish SAE feature completeness or stability.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Deliberately induced feature-steering outputs, cited findings from prior work, and routing/reconstruction metrics that do not test feature recovery or interpretation are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Toy models, near-orthogonal overlap, the sparsity transition and geometry: all untested.
The capacity account of polysemanticity is untested.
Non-capacity sources of polysemanticity are untested.
Whether features are distributed across neurons, or whether recovered SAE features reflect the model's sparse features, is not tested. The study only benchmarks SAE variants.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are untested.
Whether features are one-dimensional or multi-dimensional is untested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with V4 supports was overturned. Every row is a comparison of SAE methods, or a selected example, in a paper proposing a new SAE. This is the T4 case of relying on the finding as a tool and reporting the method's own performance. Feature counts depend on the authors' activation threshold and context filter. Interpretation scores come from 100 sampled features scored by GPT-4o, which the authors call indicative only. Steering examples are induced interventions.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap and near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The study tests whether SAEs recover interpretable features from one LLM's activations. It does not measure how features are distributed across neurons, compare against a ground-truth feature set, or establish completeness or generality across LLMs.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features as the model's units.
Whether the relevant represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RouteSAE and other SAE evaluations on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: The study reports thousands of screened interpretable SAE features and gives recognizable feature examples; RouteSAE's interpretation scores exceed 4.4 across the tested sparsity levels (r3-r4, r9-r10, r13-r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The evidence comes from this one instruct model, and the score evaluation uses a 100-feature sample with GPT-4o scoring; it does not establish that the result generalizes to other models or that the recovered features are complete (r4, r10, r13-r16).
